Front matter
blocks.content:
arXiv:hep-th/0006156v1  20 Jun 2000
STRONGLY COUPLED QUANTUM DISCRETE LIOUVILLE
THEORY. I: ALGEBRAIC APPROACH AND DUALITY
L.D. FADDEEV, R.M. KASHAEV, AND A.YU. VOLKOV
Abstract. The quantum discrete Liouville model in the strongly cou-
pled regime, 1 < c < 25, is formulated as a well deﬁned quantum me-
chanical problem with unitary evolution operator. The theory is self-
dual: there are two exponential ﬁelds related by Hermitean conjugation,
satisfying two discrete quantum Liouville equations, and living in mu-
tually commuting subalgebras of the quantum algebra of observables.

blocks.title: Recollecting the facts
blocks.content: In this section we remind in appropriate form some facts about the Liouville model and the technique of its discretization.

blocks.title: Liouville formula
Discrete Liouville equation
blocks.content: It not only ideologically justifies the chosen discretization but also helps make the following action more entertaining. In continuum, the Liouville equation may be considered as a compatibility condition for the Liouville formula overloaded with Möbius-invariance. It ought to be just the same on the lattice, so let us find out what "equation of motion" the $\chi$'s might solve. We pick four of them next to each other to figure out that they are four cross-ratios made from the total of six $\alpha$'s and $\beta$'s. blocks.title: Conclusions and comments
blocks.content:
We have shown, that the appropriate lattice regularization of the quantum Liouville model allows to enter the "forbidden region" of the Virasoro central charge $1\le c\le25$. The key for this is using the double family of dual quantum fields, which are not selfadjoint, but normal and adjoint to each other. The results are still rather modest, but proving the point quite persuasively.
